package-lock.json.label: root policy: allowlist + CC-BY-4.0
package-lock.json.reason: caniuse-lite is browser-support data under an attribution licence, reached only through eslint-plugin-unicorn > core-js-compat > browserslist, so it is a lint-time dependency that no published file carries.

tolerances.reason: sharp's platform binaries are optional dependencies that only the documentation site build loads. The site is private and ships as static HTML, and LGPL-3.0-or-later binds a redistributor of the covered library, which TEA never is. The root graph carries them because docs:build runs astro from the root. Publishing the site as a package withdraws this and the gate fails.

undeclared.evidence: zod-to-ts 1.2.0's own published package.json carries no license field, which is why npm records none in the lockfile entry; that version's manifest is silent rather than differently licensed. The registry's current top-level license field reads MIT (inherited from the 2.x line, published years later), and the repository at github.com/sachinraja/zod-to-ts carries an MIT LICENSE file whose copyright range (2021-2025) covers 1.2.0's 2023 publish date, which is the evidence that ties the reading to the locked version itself rather than to a later release.
undeclared.reason: A transitive dependency of astro 5 whose manifest declares no licence. The licence it is read as is held against the allowlist like every other entry.
